title: CORDOBA: Carbon-Efficient Optimization Framework for Computing Systems
problem: Optimizing the carbon footprint of computing systems across large hardware design spaces is intractable with existing methods because it requires simultaneously trading off operational carbon, embodied carbon, performance, power, and area (PPA) under uncertainty in carbon intensity parameters.
motivation: The semiconductor industry's contribution to global carbon emissions is growing, and neither energy-focused nor performance-focused design optimization captures the full lifecycle carbon cost, particularly embodied carbon from chip manufacturing.
method: CORDOBA introduces the total Carbon Delay Product (tCDP) metric — product of total lifecycle carbon (operational + embodied) and application execution time — as a single scalar objective for carbon-efficient hardware optimization. The framework performs design-space exploration by sweeping hardware configurations (e.g., core count, memory hierarchy, 2D vs. 3D integration via chiplet stacking) and evaluating tCDP under parametric uncertainty in carbon intensity, eliminating up to 98% of the design space as Pareto-dominated. Two case studies apply CORDOBA to real CPU systems: halving cores from 8 to 4 and adopting 3D-stacked logic+memory integration.
key_novelty: The tCDP metric that jointly captures operational carbon, embodied carbon, and performance in one optimization target, enabling principled design-space pruning for carbon-efficient specialized hardware.
contributions: Definition and justification of the total Carbon Delay Product (tCDP) as a carbon-efficiency metric that subsumes both operational and embodied carbon.
CORDOBA framework for large-scale carbon-aware hardware design-space exploration with uncertainty quantification, pruning up to 98% of configurations.
Case study showing 1.25x tCDP improvement by reducing CPU cores from 8 to 4.
Case study showing 6.9x tCDP improvement via 3D-stacked logic+memory integration versus conventional 2D systems.

metrics.other: tCDP improved 1.25x (8→4 cores); tCDP improved 6.9x (3D stacking vs. 2D); 98% design-space elimination

limitations: Carbon intensity parameters carry significant uncertainty and the framework's conclusions are sensitive to regional grid carbon assumptions not always publicly available.
primary_theme: Carbon-aware hardware design-space optimization with lifecycle carbon metrics
